items.title: Maine CDC: Childhood Vaccine Guidance Remains Unchanged Following Federal Action
items.content_text:
Aug 11, 2026
Maine will continue to follow the guidance of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) on childhood vaccine recommendations, despite President Donald Trump’s executive order on childhood vaccinations, per the Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC).
“President Trump and Secretary Kennedy are playing politics with the lives of our nation’s children. Vaccines are safe and effective and save lives,”
said Governor Janet Mills.
“Maine will continue to follow the science and the facts, and our approach to vaccines remains unchanged by yesterday’s executive order.”
“Vaccines are our most effective defense against vaccine-preventable illnesses,”
said Dr. Puthiery Va, Director of the Maine CDC.
“In Maine, vaccines remain available at no cost to eligible children through the Maine CDC’s Immunization Program. Maine’s school and child care immunization requirements remain unchanged by federal actions to date.”
As the AAP has noted in their 8/10
statement
in response to this executive order:
“Vaccine recommendations from the American Academy of Pediatrics are tailored to the health of children living in the United States and are based on decades of research and systematic tracking of real-world experiences. Pediatricians recommend children receive certain vaccines at specific ages based on when children's immune systems will respond best and when they are most vulnerable to certain diseases. Sometimes this means children will receive a single shot that protects against multiple diseases, or they may receive multiple vaccines at one visit.”
Beginning in 2021, Maine removed non-medical exemptions from the school and child care immunization requirements pursuant
Public Law 2019, Ch. 154
. That decision was upheld by a vote of 72.81 percent of Maine voters at the ballot box in 2020.

Aug 11, 2026

Maine will continue to follow the guidance of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) on childhood vaccine recommendations, despite President Donald Trump’s executive order on childhood vaccinations, per the Maine Department of Health and Human Services’ Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC).

“President Trump and Secretary Kennedy are playing politics with the lives of our nation’s children. Vaccines are safe and effective and save lives,” said Governor Janet Mills. “Maine will continue to follow the science and the facts, and our approach to vaccines remains unchanged by yesterday’s executive order.” 

“Vaccines are our most effective defense against vaccine-preventable illnesses,” said Dr. Puthiery Va, Director of the Maine CDC.“In Maine, vaccines remain available at no cost to eligible children through the Maine CDC’s Immunization Program. Maine’s school and child care immunization requirements remain unchanged by federal actions to date.”

As the AAP has noted in their 8/10 statement in response to this executive order:

 “Vaccine recommendations from the American Academy of Pediatrics are tailored to the health of children living in the United States and are based on decades of research and systematic tracking of real-world experiences. Pediatricians recommend children receive certain vaccines at specific ages based on when children's immune systems will respond best and when they are most vulnerable to certain diseases. Sometimes this means children will receive a single shot that protects against multiple diseases, or they may receive multiple vaccines at one visit.” 

Beginning in 2021, Maine removed non-medical exemptions from the school and child care immunization requirements pursuant Public Law 2019, Ch. 154. That decision was upheld by a vote of 72.81 percent of Maine voters at the ballot box in 2020.

Maine eCourts Scheduled to be Implemented in Cumberland County Courts in September

Date: 8/4/2026

The Maine Judicial Branch announced today that the schedule for transitioning courts in Cumberland County (comprising Judicial Region 2) from paper filing to electronic filing (eFiling) is scheduled for Monday, September 28, 2026. The next implementation includes all case types in the Cumberland County Unified Criminal Docket (UCD), Cumberland County Superior Court, Portland District Court, and Bridgton District Court.

Attorneys, government agencies (except law enforcement agencies), and parties who file more than six non-emergency cases in a calendar year, are required to eFile in courts that have implemented Maine eCourts. Self-represented parties are not required to eFile and can continue to file documents as they always have, in paper at the courthouse, by mail, or by email if filing a protection from abuse or harassment case.

Attorneys and other required eFilers should prepare in advance for the transition, and take note of upcoming presentation and trainings:

Presentation for Cumberland County Legal Professionals and Stakeholders
The Maine Judicial Branch will hold a virtual presentation by ZOOM on August 10th, at noon to discuss the implementation of Maine eCourts and electronic filing (eFiling) in Judicial Region 2, Cumberland County Courts. Attorneys and other professional filers are encouraged to attend.

Topic: Maine eCourts in Region 2: Cumberland County
Date & Time: Monday, August 10, 2026 at 12:00 p.m.
Please click the link below to join the webinar:
https://courts-maine-gov.zoom.us/j/94955753059
 Passcode: 993548

The webinar will be recorded and made available on the Judicial Branch website on the Maine eCourts Training & Resources page following the live session.

eFiler Trainings for Attorneys and Staff
Members of the Maine eCourts project team will conduct in-person training for attorneys and staff according to the schedule below. Please note, registration is required to attend a training session. Prosecutors and staff will receive a separate link to register by email.

  • Prosecutor eFiler Training: Session #1 - Wednesday, September 2nd at 9:00am - 4:00pm (27 Northport Drive, Portland)
  • Prosecutor eFiler Training: Session #2 Thursday, September 3rd at 9:00am - 4:00pm (27 Northport Drive, Portland)
  • All Other eFiler Training: Session #1 Thursday, September 10th at 9:00am - 1:00pm (York Judicial Center, Biddeford) Register for this session
  • All Other eFiler Training: Session #2 Friday, September 11th at 9:00am - 1:00pm (York Judicial Center, Biddeford) Register for this session

About Maine eCourts
Maine eCourts is a suite of applications and web-based tools provided by Tyler Technologies' Enterprise Justice Software. The system allows for the management of court dockets and hearings, storage of digital case files, eFiling, and online payments.

For more information about Maine eCourts visit: https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html. To receive updates from the Maine Judicial Branch on Maine eCourts and other news, sign up for our mailing list at: https://www.courts.maine.gov/news/signup.html

items.content_text:
STATE OF MAINE 
SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT 
STANDING ORDER ON SERVICEMEMBERS OR SPOUSES OF SERVICEMEMBERS 
SEEKING ADMISSION TO THE MAINE BAR 
 
Effective August 3, 2026 
Attorneys who are servicemembers or spouses of servicemembers 
assigned to Maine and who wish to be licensed in Maine while they or their 
spouses are stationed here may seek waiver of strict compliance with the 
duration of practice requirement of the rule g overning admission by motion 
without examination, Maine Bar Admission Rule 11A(a)(2).  The Maine 
Supreme Judicial Court, the Maine Board of Overseers of the Bar, and the Maine 
Board of Bar Examiners are committed to working with these applicants to 
accommodate their unique circumstances and to expedite the bar application 
process to the extent possible when they or their spouses’ service brings them 
to Maine. 
The Court will consider requests for waiver on a case -by-case basis, 
depending on the individual circumstances of the applicant.   Servicemembers 
and spouses of servicemembers are encouraged to contact the Maine Supreme 
Judicial Court Clerk’s Office at (207)822-4146 for more information about the 
waiver process. Servicemembers and spouses of servicemembers assigned to 
Maine who wish to take the Maine bar examination but have missed a deadline 
to apply for the exam, should also contact the Maine Board of Bar Examiners at 
(207)623-2464 or execdir@mainebarexaminers.org for assistance. 
Promulgation Date: 8/3/2026 FOR THE COURT: 
 
 
   /s/      
VALERIE STANFILL

Competitive Skills Scholarship Program (CSSP) Rule Changes Effective August 2, 2026

August 5, 2026

The Maine Department of Labor has updated the Competitive Skills Scholarship Program (CSSP) rules to implement recent statutory changes, expand participant supports, improve program flexibility, and clarify program requirements. The revised rules took effect on August 2, 2026.

Some of the most significant changes include:

  • Expanded monthly stipend eligibility. More students may now qualify for a monthly CSSP stipend because income eligibility limits have increased.
  • Partial stipends for part-time students. Eligible part-time students may now receive a prorated monthly stipend based on their enrollment status and income.
  • Expanded support services. Eligible participants may qualify for increased assistance with transportation, vehicle repairs, and other necessary needs under higher support service funding limits.
  • Expanded educational opportunities. Eligibility has also been expanded for applicants with pre-existing preparatory associate degree programs.
  • Improved program clarity and accessibility. The revised rules simplify eligibility requirements, clarify appeal rights, improve communication preferences, and increase transparency regarding the High-Wage, In-Demand Occupations list.
  • New CSSP Cohort funding opportunities. Training providers and their partners will be invited to apply for CSSP Cohort funding. The Maine Department of Labor will host a listening session to gather feedback on implementation before issuing a Request for Applications (RFA) for pilot cohort programs.

For those interested in reviewing the complete rule changes, including the final adopted rule, tracked changes, and the Department's Summary of Comments and Responses from the rulemaking process, please visit the Maine Department of Labor Rulemaking webpage: https://www.maine.gov/labor/rulemaking/

CSSP Cohort Listening Session

Community members interested in learning more about the CSSP Cohort model are invited to join a listening session on September 18th, at 10:00 a.m. to share ideas, discuss opportunities to expand access, and help identify implementation priorities.

Zoom Registration: https://mainestate.zoom.us/meeting/register/-vPlt9ZbSG23mGKG96bmsg

Current CSSP participants will receive a separate email describing the rule changes and inviting them to schedule a meeting with their CSSP case manager to review whether they may qualify for additional benefits under the new rules.

Thank you for your continued partnership in helping Maine people access education, training, and employment through the Competitive Skills Scholarship Program.

The Maine Department of Labor
